title: The leak scan flags the EC armor label quoted before a repository path that has a digit or an upper-case letter
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits does not flag the EC armor label quoted alone with a repository path on the next line when the path holds a digit or an upper-case letter (the sql2022-views.md page of mecm and the Win32.md page of Intune apps), as it does not for a lower-case path with no digit

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e)
        sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
paths = ["kb/public/mecm/sql2022-views.md", "kb/public/Intune/Apps/Win32.md"]
flagged = [p for p in paths if hit(arm + "\n" + p)]
print("armor label quoted before a repository path that is flagged:", flagged)
sys.exit(1 if flagged else 0)

        print("check failed:", e)
        sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import sys

import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
assert hit(arm + "\nAb12Cd34\nZy98Wx76\nQw45Er67"), "a narrow-wrapped EC key body with no // is no longer flagged"
assert not hit(arm + "\nkb/public/a/b.md"), "the EC armor label quoted before a plain repository path is flagged"

clauses.clause: kbcommon.leak_hits does not flag the EC armor label quoted alone with a repository path on the next line when the path holds a digit or an upper-case letter (the sql2022-views.md page of mecm and the Win32.md page of Intune apps), as it does not for a lower-case path with no digit

notes: Found by the SP-swavez3g review (S3) of BG-ok4itunr: the path rule covers only lowercase paths with no digit (the gate option taken provisionally). Three 8+ letter prose lines after the label are flagged too; decide whether that is wanted.
